2010-04-20: An explosion on the Deepwater Horizon drilling rig killed 11 men and sent millions of gallons of oil gushing into the Gulf of Mexico.
2010-04-22: The Deepwater Horizon oil rig, drilling BP's Macondo project, sank in the Gulf of Mexico after burning for 36 hours, with 11 workers missing and a major oil spill risk looming.
2010-04-23: No oil appeared to be leaking from a drilling rig that exploded and sank in the Gulf of Mexico , the Coast Guard said Friday , though officials were trying to contain what spilled after the blast and prevent any threat to the coast 's fragile ecosystem .
2010-04-26: BP vowed to pay all necessary and appropriate clean-up costs from the massive oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico.
2010-04-27: BP reported a 135% jump in first-quarter profits to $5.6bn, but its results were overshadowed by the Deepwater Horizon rig disaster, with around 1,000 barrels of oil a day still leaking into the Gulf of Mexico and 1,000 people involved in efforts to stop the leak and deal with the growing oil spill.
2010-04-28: Crews began a test burn of oil from the leaking Deepwater Horizon well in the Gulf of Mexico as part of an effort to prevent the spill from reaching the coast.
2010-04-29: The US coastguard says 5,000 barrels a day of oil are spewing from the blown-out Deepwater Horizon well, five times more than previously estimated.
2010-04-30: Oil from the Deepwater Horizon rig explosion reaches the US coast as BP struggles to contain the spill.
The US administration bans oil drilling in new areas of the US coast while the cause of the BP oil spill off Louisiana is investigated .
2010-05-02: BP begins drilling a relief well intended to permanently plug the leaking Gulf of Mexico oil well, a process estimated to take about three months.
2010-05-04: BP warns that the cost of tackling the Gulf of Mexico oil spill exceeds $6m per day and begins drilling a relief well that could take around three months, as its shares fall nearly 5%.
2010-05-05: The Obama administration takes defensive action over early assurances that a sunken BP rig was not leaking crude oil into the Gulf of Mexico, issuing a timeline of its actions and dispatching officials to the region, as BP registers its first success in plugging one of the leaks.
2010-05-07: The BP oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico continues to spread, with around 5,000 barrels leaking daily from the uncapped well following the Deepwater Horizon drilling rig accident, prompting comparisons to the Exxon Valdez disaster.
2010-05-08: A containment device lowered over the leaking BP well in the Gulf of Mexico had to be moved after ice-like crystals began accumulating inside it.
2010-05-10: BP continues to explore multiple approaches, including a "top hat" containment box, a "top kill" valve stack, and a "junk shot," to stop the oil spill from the Deepwater Horizon well in the Gulf of Mexico.

BP America CEO Lamar McKay told a Senate hearing that the company's contingency plan for the Gulf of Mexico oil spill had worked, while executives of BP, Transocean, and Halliburton blamed each other for the disaster.
BP says the Gulf of Mexico oil spill has cost it $350 million so far, with the final bill expected to be much higher.
Early finger-pointing erupted among companies involved in the Gulf of Mexico oil rig explosion and unstopped leak, on the eve of the first congressional hearings into the accident.
2010-05-12: BP says a new smaller steel "top hat" dome has been placed beside the damaged Gulf of Mexico oil well and should be working by the end of the week.
A congressional hearing was told that BP, Transocean, and Halliburton ignored tests indicating faulty safety equipment hours before the Deepwater Horizon explosion.
2010-05-13: BP releases underwater video footage showing oil and gas leaking from the Deepwater Horizon rig into the Gulf of Mexico.
2010-05-15: The US government demands immediate clarification from BP over its commitment to pay for costs caused by the Gulf of Mexico oil spill, seeking assurance BP will not limit payments to a $75m statutory cap.

The US Environmental Protection Agency approves BP's use of the toxic chemical dispersant Corexit 9500 in deep-water efforts to mitigate the Gulf of Mexico oil spill, despite warnings from Louisiana officials and scientists that the untested technique may harm marine life.
2010-05-24: The US government toughened its rhetoric toward BP over its inability to plug the leaking Gulf of Mexico oil well, with Interior Secretary Ken Salazar pledging to "keep our boot on their neck until the job gets done," while BP pledged $500m to study the spill's environmental impact.
BP plans to attempt a "top kill" procedure this week to stop the flow of oil from its ruptured Gulf of Mexico well, giving it only a 60 to 70 percent chance of success.
2010-05-27: BP's "top kill" effort has stabilized the wellhead, though it is too early to declare success, as US scientists estimate the oil leak is much worse than previously thought, making it the nation's worst spill.
Cleanup and containment efforts continue at the Gulf of Mexico site of the oil spill following the Deepwater Horizon explosion.
2010-05-28: Federal health officials call on BP to protect the health of workers cleaning up the Gulf of Mexico oil spill and residents along the coast, outlining government steps to respond to emerging health problems.
2010-05-29: BP announces that its "top kill" operation to halt the Gulf of Mexico oil leak has failed, and the company is shifting to a new strategy.
2010-05-30: BP began preparations to cut a leaking drill pipe and attach a containment cap after failing to plug the Macondo well, as the Obama administration warned oil could gush into the Gulf of Mexico until August.
2010-06-01: The US Justice Department launches criminal and civil investigations into the BP oil spill as BP's market value falls 15 percent in a day.

BP launches an operation using undersea robots to cut a damaged pipe and lower a containment cap, hoping to contain the Gulf of Mexico oil spill within 24 hours, as US officials announce criminal and civil investigations.
BP shares plunge 17 percent in London trading, wiping $23 billion off its market value, on news its latest attempt to plug the well has failed.
2010-06-02: BP uses underwater robots to slice through a pipe at the Deepwater Horizon oil spill site as part of efforts to cap the leak, though the saw became stuck during the process.
2010-06-03: Eleven workers cleaning up oil from BP's blown-out well have been treated for respiratory problems, headaches and nausea that could have been caused by burning crude oil, noxious fumes or dispersants, though BP and Coast Guard officials say dehydration, heat, food poisoning or other unrelated factors may be responsible.

The BP oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico threatens billions of dollars in tourism and fishing industries along the Gulf Coast, with oyster beds closed, shrimpers shut down, and beach communities from New Orleans to Key West bracing for impact.
2010-06-07: Nordea sells all its shares in BP, accusing the oil giant of a lack of transparency over the US oil spill, and halts further investment in BP until further notice.
2010-06-08: BP published key energy data amid its ongoing struggle to manage the Deepwater Horizon oil spill.

Cleanup efforts for the BP oil spill rely mostly on tedious manual labor, with workers picking up tar balls by hand and wiping oil off marsh grass, while BP offers cleanup jobs at $12 an hour amid curtailed fishing.
2010-06-16: Under pressure from President Obama, BP agreed to set up a $20 billion fund for claims from the Gulf of Mexico oil spill and suspended dividend payments.
2010-06-17: BP signs a letter of intent to purchase Kevin Costner's oil-cleaning machines to help clean up the Gulf of Mexico oil spill.
BP CEO Tony Hayward testifies before a House subcommittee about the Deepwater Horizon explosion and oil spill, saying the spill 'never should have happened' and that he is 'deeply sorry.'
2010-06-18: BP Chairman Carl-Henric Svanberg says CEO Tony Hayward is handing over daily operations of the Gulf oil spill response to Managing Director Bob Dudley, though other BP officials say the switch was previously announced and Hayward remains in charge until the leak is capped.
BP denies Anadarko Petroleum's claims that its handling of the Gulf of Mexico oil spill amounted to "gross negligence."
2010-06-19: BP CEO Tony Hayward faced fresh criticism for attending a yacht race with his son instead of dealing with the Gulf of Mexico oil spill.

Anadarko Petroleum, a partner in the ruptured Deepwater Horizon well, refuses to accept any blame for the BP oil spill and says BP should foot the entire bill for the cleanup, alleging BP's actions probably amounted to gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
2010-06-21: BP advanced toward permanently killing the source of the Gulf of Mexico oil spill and made a $3 billion deposit to start a $20 billion compensation fund.
BP Chairman Carl-Henric Svanberg sidelined CEO Tony Hayward, transitioning day-to-day handling of the oil spill cleanup to Managing Director Robert Dudley .
2010-06-22: Public health officials and scientists are scheduled to begin a two-day meeting in New Orleans, organized by the Institute of Medicine at the request of the Department of Health and Human Services, to discuss health effects of the BP oil spill.
2010-06-23: BP was forced to remove the containment cap from the Deepwater Horizon well after a vent was inadvertently closed, allowing oil to flow freely into the Gulf of Mexico before the cap was successfully reinstalled later that day.
House Democrats have begun drafting legislation to tighten oil industry practices, especially in deep-water drilling, in response to the BP oil spill.

BP appointed American executive Bob Dudley to head the newly created Gulf Coast Restoration Organisation, taking over management of the oil spill crisis response and clean-up from chief executive Tony Hayward.
2010-06-24: The Obama administration appeals a court ruling that blocked its six-month moratorium on deep-water drilling following the BP oil spill.
2010-06-25: BP's bill for containing and cleaning up the Gulf of Mexico oil spill climbed to $2.35bn, causing its shares to hit a 14-year low.
2010-07-05: BP says the Gulf of Mexico oil spill has cost it $3.12bn to date, with the total likely to be much higher.
2010-07-06: A Deepwater Horizon rig worker tells the BBC he identified a leak in the rig's safety equipment weeks before the explosion that caused the Gulf of Mexico oil spill, and that both BP and Transocean were informed but the faulty device was shut down rather than fixed.
2010-07-10: Engineers removed the LMRP cap from the Deepwater Horizon well, allowing oil to flow freely from the blowout preventer again, and then bolted on a new capping stack to conduct tests on stopping the flow.
2010-07-13: Engineers begin testing a new containment cap on BP's leaking Gulf of Mexico wellhead to determine whether it can withstand pressure and temporarily halt the oil flow.
2010-07-14: The federal government raises concerns about BP's plan to test a new containment cap on the Gulf of Mexico well, delaying the operation and prompting BP to temporarily halt drilling of relief wells.
2010-07-15: BP and government experts are considering whether to carry out a "static kill" operation on the damaged well, as bad weather in the Gulf could force ships to withdraw and halt relief well work for up to two weeks.
The leak from the Deepwater Horizon well in the Gulf of Mexico was capped, ending 87 days of oil spilling into the sea.
2010-07-20: BP agrees to sell $7 billion in assets to Apache Corp as part of its planned $10 billion asset sale to pay for the Gulf of Mexico oil spill.
2010-07-21: BP agrees to sell $7bn in assets to contribute towards a $20bn fund to compensate those affected by the Gulf of Mexico oil spill.
2010-07-25: BP chief executive Tony Hayward has been negotiating the terms of his exit, with a formal announcement likely within 24 hours, amid criticism over his handling of the Gulf of Mexico oil spill.
BP is set to reveal that an internal inquiry has cleared it of gross negligence in the Deepwater Horizon explosion and oil spill, while expecting evidence of other companies' and contractors' roles.
2010-07-27: BP chief executive Tony Hayward announces his resignation in the aftermath of the Gulf of Mexico oil spill, with a payoff of about £1m and a pension expected to be about £500,000 a year.
2010-07-30: Activists and professors at UC Berkeley stage an anti-BP demonstration and call for severing the university's research partnership with BP over its catastrophic Gulf of Mexico oil spill.
2010-08-03: BP begins its "static kill" procedure, pumping heavy mud and cement into the Macondo well to try to permanently seal the source of the Gulf of Mexico oil spill.
2010-08-04: The US government says most of the oil that leaked into the Gulf of Mexico has been cleaned up, as BP reports its "static kill" procedure is holding back the flow of crude.
2010-08-09: BP made an initial deposit of $3bn into a $20bn compensation fund for the Gulf of Mexico oil spill after completing talks with the US Department of Justice.
2010-08-11: BP is investigating several hundred compensation claims related to the Gulf of Mexico oil spill, with fears that some payments may be fraudulent.
2010-08-13: Alabama sues BP, Transocean and Halliburton for "catastrophic harm" caused by the Gulf of Mexico oil spill, becoming the first state to sue BP over the disaster.
2010-08-15: The BP oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico has reawakened painful memories for people who lived through what was America's worst spill - until now - in the once-bountiful waters of southern Alaska.
2010-08-16: The Obama administration calls for environmental reviews for all new deepwater oil drilling after a White House report found BP received environmental exemptions based on decades-old data for its Gulf of Mexico well.
2010-08-23: Kenneth Feinberg, the independent administrator of BP's Gulf Coast Claims Facility, pledged swift and generous compensation payments to victims of the BP oil spill, but said claimants must give up their right to sue BP.
2010-08-25: A BP executive testified that the blowout preventer's plumbing was connected improperly, with a line meant for a cutting ram instead connected to a test ram, and that a work-around effort also failed to contain the well.
2010-08-26: Galicia's recovery from the 2002 Prestige oil disaster is cited as a potential inspiration for those pessimistic about recovery from the BP oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico.
2010-09-03: BP says the cost of its Gulf of Mexico oil spill has risen to $8bn, with about $399m paid out in claims and permanent sealing of the well expected later in September.
The 450-ton blowout preventer from BP's Macondo well is removed from the Gulf of Mexico floor to be hauled to the surface as federal evidence in the investigation of the BP oil spill.
2010-09-08: BP releases a report on the Deepwater Horizon disaster that spreads blame for the largest offshore oil spill in history, citing a series of failures including weaknesses in cement design and testing and the rig crew's incorrect view that a pressure test was successful.
2010-09-10: BP delays publication of its third-quarter results by a week due to the complexity of accounting for the Gulf of Mexico oil spill.
2010-09-13: BP's incoming CEO Bob Dudley indicated that compensation claims related to the Gulf of Mexico oil spill will likely be less than the $20 billion the company placed into an independent claims fund.
2010-09-17: BP's Macondo oil well is declared physically incapable of leaking further after a relief well intercepts it and cement is pumped in during a "bottom kill" operation.
2010-09-19: BP permanently sealed the Macondo well in the Gulf of Mexico by pumping cement into the undersea reserve and intercepting the leaking well with a relief well, ending the five-month oil spill.
2010-09-27: The chairmen of the president's Oil Spill Commission expressed skepticism about claims from BP and government officials that initial underestimation of the Macondo well's flow rate had no impact on the response to the Deepwater Horizon spill.
2010-09-28: A Gallup survey of nearly 2,600 Gulf Coast residents found depression cases rose more than 25 percent after the BP oil spill, though the study did not conclude the additional cases were directly tied to the oil.
2010-09-29: BP's new chief executive Bob Dudley ousted the company's chief of exploration and production, Andy Inglis, in the wake of the massive Gulf of Mexico oil spill and divided his responsibilities among three other BP executives.
2010-10-01: BP pledges revenues from several Gulf of Mexico oil fields, including Thunder Horse, Atlantis and Mad Dog, to help finance its $20 billion compensation fund for victims of the oil spill.
2010-10-06: A judge orders an eight-week trial starting February 27, 2012, to determine blame among BP, Transocean, and other defendants for the Gulf oil spill.
2010-10-20: BP has paid nearly $2.5 billion to people and businesses affected by the oil spill.
2010-10-25: BP chief executive Bob Dudley says the company will not quit the United States despite the Deepwater Horizon oil spill and is rebuilding trust after the Gulf of Mexico environmental crisis .
2010-10-28: A White House panel said Halliburton used flawed cement in BP's doomed Gulf of Mexico well that could have contributed to the blowout that sparked the worst offshore oil spill in U.S. history.
2010-11-02: BP increased its financial provision for the Gulf of Mexico oil spill by $8 billion, raising its estimate of the total cost to $40 billion.
2010-11-09: Drilling experts and corporate rivals testifying before a presidential oil spill commission criticized BP's decisions about the Deepwater Horizon drilling rig that may have contributed to the April 20 blowout and the massive Gulf of Mexico oil spill.
2010-11-16: The deadline for Gulf oil spill victims to file claims for short-term damages from BP PLC is 11:59 p.m. Tuesday.
2010-11-24: The administrator of BP's $20-billion Gulf Coast Claims Facility, Kenneth Feinberg, stopped accepting emergency claims and began accepting final settlements for victims of the BP oil spill, encouraging claimants to file early for more generous terms.
2010-12-02: The White House oil spill commission said that bad management and a communications breakdown by BP and its Macondo well partners caused the Gulf of Mexico oil disaster, labeling BP's safety lapses "chronic" and saying the fatal blowout could have been avoided.
2010-12-14: The U.S. Justice Department is expected to announce as early as Wednesday its first significant legal action, involving civil lawsuits rather than criminal charges, stemming from the BP oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico.
2010-12-15: The Justice Department sued BP and eight other companies over the Gulf of Mexico oil disaster, seeking civil penalties under the Clean Water Act and another federal statute for cleanup costs and environmental damage.
2011-01-05: The White House oil spill commission concluded that BP and its partners made cost-cutting decisions that contributed to the Gulf of Mexico oil spill.
2011-01-06: The National Oil Spill Commission finds that the Deepwater Horizon blowout and BP oil spill were "avoidable" and resulted from a failure of management by BP and its contractors.
2011-01-11: The presidential oil spill commission calls for tougher federal regulation, stiffer fines, and a new industry-run safety organization in response to the BP oil spill.
2011-01-24: A Florida lawmaker introduces a bill aimed at blocking Cuba from drilling a new deepwater oil well off its northern coast, citing threats from a potential oil spill like the BP Deepwater Horizon disaster.
2011-01-31: BP's compensation fund for Gulf oil spill victims has issued a final settlement payment to just one of the thousands of people and businesses waiting for checks, and that $10 million payout went to a company after BP intervened on its behalf.
